simplechallenges.guide.page.1.title: Simple Challenges
simplechallenges.guide.page.1: Game modes for a world of your choice. First the Unlock mode: the world is cut into cells and only free cells can be entered; you pay to open the next one. Without a chosen challenge the mod changes nothing.
simplechallenges.guide.page.2.title: Simple Challenges
simplechallenges.guide.page.2: Open this guide again with /simplechallenges guide.
simplechallenges.guide.page.3.title: Safety lock
simplechallenges.guide.page.3: Without a chosen challenge Simple Challenges changes nothing: no state file is written, the collision and block hooks return at once and no tick work runs.
simplechallenges.guide.page.4.title: Safety lock
simplechallenges.guide.page.4: A challenge exists only in a world whose state says so.
simplechallenges.guide.page.5.title: Safety lock
simplechallenges.guide.page.5: It is chosen by the server option defaultChallenge for a brand-new world, or, in test worlds, by a game master with /simplechallenges activate after allowAdminCommands was switched on (off by default).
simplechallenges.guide.page.6.title: Safety lock
simplechallenges.guide.page.6: The Enable Simple Challenges switch of SimpleBuilding and the mod's own enabled option close the gate again at any time.
simplechallenges.guide.page.7.title: Unlock grid
simplechallenges.guide.page.7: The Overworld is cut into square columns of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (a chunk), 32 or 48 blocks (three chunks) over the full height. Only free cells can be entered:
simplechallenges.guide.page.8.title: Unlock grid
simplechallenges.guide.page.8: every entity, players, mobs, items, vehicles and projectiles, stops at a locked cell like at a wall, without a border entity or rubber banding, and slides along it.
simplechallenges.guide.page.9.title: Unlock grid
simplechallenges.guide.page.9: Blocks in locked cells cannot be changed (players, pistons, fluids, growth, explosions).
simplechallenges.guide.page.10.title: Unlock grid
simplechallenges.guide.page.10: Anyone found inside a locked cell (teleport, ender pearl, respawn, spawn) is brought to the nearest free cell. Creative and spectator players may pass if exemptCreative is on.
simplechallenges.guide.page.11.title: Border line
simplechallenges.guide.page.11: Clients with the mod get the free cells from the server (everything at join, one cell per unlock) and see the edge of the free area as a line of red dust near them.
simplechallenges.guide.page.12.title: Border line
simplechallenges.guide.page.12: /simplechallenges border switches the line on and off on your client. The client uses the same collision as the server, so walking against the border feels like a wall.
simplechallenges.guide.page.13.title: Prices
simplechallenges.guide.page.13: Every cell next to the free area has a price, worked out once from the world seed, the cell and what the world offers there, and then kept in the world state.
simplechallenges.guide.page.14.title: Prices
simplechallenges.guide.page.14: Easy: an item the free area gives by hand (dirt, sand, logs of a tree at the start).
simplechallenges.guide.page.15.title: Prices
simplechallenges.guide.page.15: Medium: an item of the cell's own surroundings. Hard: a ladder from cobblestone through coal, iron, gold to diamonds by how many cells are free.
simplechallenges.guide.page.16.title: Prices
simplechallenges.guide.page.16: Block-by-block unlock (cell size 1) prices a column by the value of its blocks (data/simplechallenges/simplechallenges/block_value.json). The amount grows with the cell edge and is capped at two stacks.
simplechallenges.guide.page.17.title: Prices
simplechallenges.guide.page.17: The currency is items, credits or experience levels. Looking at the world never generates a chunk.
simplechallenges.guide.page.18.title: Credits from advancements
simplechallenges.guide.page.18: With credits as currency, every advancement that shows a toast and is not a root or recipe advancement pays credits once for the whole team (or, with the server option perPlayerCredits, once for each player
simplechallenges.guide.page.19.title: Credits from advancements
simplechallenges.guide.page.19: into a pot of their own): task 1, goal 2, challenge 5 (changeable in the preset). Advancements a player already had when they were first seen count as the baseline and pay nothing.
simplechallenges.guide.page.20.title: Credits from advancements
simplechallenges.guide.page.21.title: Deadlock protection
simplechallenges.guide.page.21: When a challenge starts and after every unlock the mod checks that at least one cell next to the free area can be paid with something the free area offers.
simplechallenges.guide.page.22.title: Deadlock protection
simplechallenges.guide.page.22: If not, one cell gets a replacement price from the area's own items, or a single level if the area offers nothing.
simplechallenges.guide.page.23.title: Deadlock protection
simplechallenges.guide.page.23: In addition, when nothing was unlocked for the preset's pity time (default 30 minutes while someone is online) and nothing can be paid, or credits are used up, the cell nearest to the origin opens for free.
simplechallenges.guide.page.24.title: Deadlock protection
simplechallenges.guide.page.25.title: Presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.25: A challenge is a preset file: data/<namespace>/simplechallenges/preset/<id>.json in a mod or data pack, or config/simplechallenges/presets/<id>.json of your own.
simplechallenges.guide.page.26.title: Presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.26: The loader checks everything (cell size 1 to 48, start rectangles in cell units up to 4096 cells, currency, price tier, dimensions, pity time, credits per frame) and shows readable problems instead of crashing;
simplechallenges.guide.page.27.title: Presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.27: modes planned for later stages load with a note but cannot be started. A world keeps a copy of the preset it started with. Shipped:
simplechallenges.guide.page.28.title: Presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.28: Vanilla Unlock (chunks), Block by Block, Quick Steps (three chunks), Trophy Land (credits from advancements), Classic Skyblock, Sky One Block, Sky Grid and Island Unlock (island with cells).
simplechallenges.guide.page.29.title: Commands
simplechallenges.guide.page.29: /simplechallenges (status) shows the challenge, free cells, credits and the price of the cell you look at. /simplechallenges unlock pays for the cell in your line of sight (or /simplechallenges unlock <x> <z>).
simplechallenges.guide.page.30.title: Commands
simplechallenges.guide.page.30: /simplechallenges presets lists the presets and problems. Game masters, only when allowAdminCommands is on: activate <preset>, deactivate, credits add <n>, unlock <x> <z> free. Client:
simplechallenges.guide.page.31.title: Commands
simplechallenges.guide.page.31: /simplechallenges guide opens this handbook, /simplechallenges border toggles the border line. /simplechallenges config sets the server options.
simplechallenges.guide.page.32.title: World creation
simplechallenges.guide.page.32: The world type button of the Create New World screen offers Simple Challenges next to Superflat. Chosen, the World tab shows the challenge, three buttons with the challenges played last (first start:
simplechallenges.guide.page.33.title: World creation
simplechallenges.guide.page.33: Classic Skyblock, Sky One Block, Vanilla Unlock) and Select Challenge.
simplechallenges.guide.page.34.title: World creation
simplechallenges.guide.page.34: That screen lists the shipped presets and your own, with a picture of each (start area map, island from above, block ladder, grid), and Play Challenge fixes the choice for the world that Create New World makes.
simplechallenges.guide.page.35.title: World creation
simplechallenges.guide.page.35: Duplicate makes a copy of your own that you can change:
simplechallenges.guide.page.36.title: World creation
simplechallenges.guide.page.36: name, cell size, price, price tier and the start area, which you paint as rectangles on a map (left drag adds, right drag removes, middle drag moves, wheel zooms;
simplechallenges.guide.page.37.title: World creation
simplechallenges.guide.page.37: the spawn cell always stays). Own presets are files in config/simplechallenges/presets/. Leaving the screen or choosing another world type drops the choice. A Skyblock preset makes the Overworld a void world.
simplechallenges.guide.page.38.title: Skyblock family
simplechallenges.guide.page.38: Three world modes start in the void and can be combined with the Unlock mode. Classic Skyblock builds a start island at the spawn (styles classic, mini and desert) with a chest and a tree or cactus.
simplechallenges.guide.page.39.title: Skyblock family
simplechallenges.guide.page.39: Sky One Block puts one grass block at 0,0; mined, it grows back within a quarter second with the next block of a sequence that picks from ever richer phases (every 40 blocks a new one: meadow, stone age, caves, deep, nether, end).
simplechallenges.guide.page.40.title: Skyblock family
simplechallenges.guide.page.40: Sky Grid puts a block every 4 blocks in all three directions (kind picked from a weighted list by the world seed) into every new chunk; a platform at the spawn is left free. Island Unlock combines the island with cells of 2 blocks:
simplechallenges.guide.page.41.title: Skyblock family
simplechallenges.guide.page.41: only the middle of the island is free at first, and the island's own items (dirt, wood, leaves) pay for the next cells. Nether and End stay Vanilla.
simplechallenges.guide.page.42.title: Spawn, edges and the crosshair line
simplechallenges.guide.page.42: A challenge chosen for a brand-new world fixes the world spawn at block 0,0 without the Vanilla scatter, so the start always lies inside the start area (a world that was already played keeps its spawn).
simplechallenges.guide.page.43.title: Spawn, edges and the crosshair line
simplechallenges.guide.page.43: No new mob appears in a locked cell. A sneaking player may lean a quarter of a block over the border to build at the edge.
simplechallenges.guide.page.44.title: Spawn, edges and the crosshair line
simplechallenges.guide.page.44: Looking at a locked cell next to the free area shows a line under the crosshair:
simplechallenges.guide.page.45.title: Spawn, edges and the crosshair line
simplechallenges.guide.page.45: the price, how much you have, and whether you can pay it (pay with /simplechallenges unlock).
simplechallenges.guide.page.46.title: Lucky Block and Random Drops
simplechallenges.guide.page.46: In a Lucky challenge a block you break drops another block instead of itself. Common blocks come up more often than rare ones:
simplechallenges.guide.page.47.title: Lucky Block and Random Drops
simplechallenges.guide.page.47: the chance of a block is its commonness divided by (rarity value + 1) to the power alpha (default 1.3),
simplechallenges.guide.page.48.title: Lucky Block and Random Drops
simplechallenges.guide.page.48: both read from block_value.json, so stone is far more likely than a diamond ore and a Netherite block almost never
simplechallenges.guide.page.49.title: Lucky Block and Random Drops
simplechallenges.guide.page.49: comes. The first six blocks of a world (the pity) give wood and stone so nobody starts without tools. Random Drops swaps every block for one fixed other block per world seed instead of rolling anew.
simplechallenges.guide.page.50.title: Lucky Block and Random Drops
simplechallenges.guide.page.50: Creative players, blocks with contents such as chests, and breaks that would drop nothing anyway (wrong tool) stay Vanilla. Lucky combines with Unlock (Lucky Land) and with the One Block (Lucky One Block).
simplechallenges.guide.page.51.title: Skyline Block
simplechallenges.guide.page.51: The world is void and single blocks float in the air with one block of air between them, in a fixed order per dimension:
simplechallenges.guide.page.52.title: Skyline Block
simplechallenges.guide.page.52: the Overworld line starts with grass, dirt and wood and ends with Obsidian (the portal block), the Nether line holds all Nether blocks, the End line all End blocks.
simplechallenges.guide.page.53.title: Skyline Block
simplechallenges.guide.page.53: Linear lays them along +X, Grid fills the positive quarter in shells on every second coordinate, Ring winds in layers round the start. A block you break grows back at once, so the line is endless.
simplechallenges.guide.page.54.title: Skyline Block
simplechallenges.guide.page.54: Blocks that cannot stand alone (torches, plants, doors, rails, ladders) get a Bedrock support, falling blocks one below. Arriving in a dimension puts you on its first block: there is no platform and no portal destination of its own;
simplechallenges.guide.page.55.title: Skyline Block
simplechallenges.guide.page.55: in the End the main island and the dragon stay Vanilla and the line starts at the place of the arrival platform. The Nether line ends in a Bedrock seal:
simplechallenges.guide.page.56.title: Skyline Block
simplechallenges.guide.page.56: hit it with a Netherite pickaxe while holding an Eye of Ender in the other hand to open it, and an End portal stands next to it. The chunks get their blocks while they are generated; nothing is scanned.
simplechallenges.guide.page.57.title: Easter eggs of the Skyline
simplechallenges.guide.page.57: In the linear and the grid Skyline (never the ring) a loot structure waits in -X, where no line block stands:
simplechallenges.guide.page.58.title: Easter eggs of the Skyline
simplechallenges.guide.page.58: in the End a small ship with an Elytra in a frame, in the Nether a mini bastion whose chest always holds a Netherite upgrade smithing template, in the Overworld a vault that gives a Heavy Core and a frame with a trial key.
simplechallenges.guide.page.59.title: Easter eggs of the Skyline
simplechallenges.guide.page.59: The Elytra and the key come back whenever someone takes them; the vault is the Vanilla vault, every player opens it once.
simplechallenges.guide.page.60.title: Easter eggs of the Skyline
simplechallenges.guide.page.60: Each egg exists twice at the same distance from the start (96 blocks, 190 in the End), the second one 30 degrees aside, in case the first is destroyed. A structure is built when the chunk of its place is generated.
simplechallenges.guide.page.61.title: Easter eggs of the Skyline
simplechallenges.guide.page.61: The shipped Skyline presets have the eggs on (easterEggs in the preset).
simplechallenges.guide.page.62.title: The 16 presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.63.title: The 16 presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.63: Vanilla Unlock (a chunk per cell), Block by Block (a single block per cell), Quick Steps (three chunks per cell), Trophy Land (advancements give credits), Island Unlock (Skyblock with unlockable cells), Classic Skyblock, Sky One Block, Sky Grid,
simplechallenges.guide.page.64.title: The 16 presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.64: Lucky Strike (broken blocks drop other blocks), Lucky Land (Lucky with Unlock), Lucky One Block, Random Drops (every block always drops the same other block), Skyline Block (one line), Skyline Grid, Skyline Ring and One Line (a one chunk
simplechallenges.guide.page.65.title: The 16 presets
simplechallenges.guide.page.65: wide corridor to unlock along). Everything is a preset file, so you can copy one and change it.
simplechallenges.guide.page.66.title: Settings
simplechallenges.guide.page.66: More settings are in the mod's config screen.
